persistence.rationale: Documented sustained organizing across the Delano Grape Strike (1965-1970, five full years to resolution) and continuing boycott/lobbying work into the 1970s (lettuce, Gallo wine, table grapes) and beyond -- a multi-decade documented pattern, not one campaign.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Documented continued public protest activity that led to a severe police beating at a 1988 San Francisco protest (two fractured ribs, ruptured spleen) -- did not withdraw from public organizing afterward, corroborated by the resulting $825,000 settlement record.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Inferred from sustained, decades-long public confrontational organizing (strikes, boycotts, protests) at real, documented physical cost (the 1988 beating) -- scored dual-edged given that cost was real and severe, not merely reputational.

achievement_drive.rationale: Inferred from co-founding the National Farm Workers Association (1962) and personally negotiating the labor contracts that concluded the 1970 Delano strike, then successfully lobbying for California's 1975 Agricultural Labor Relations Act -- the first state law of its kind, a specific, dated legislative achievement.

leadership_drive.rationale: Documented as co-founder (with Cesar Chavez and Gilbert Padilla) of the organization that became the United Farm Workers, and as personally organizing East Coast boycott campaigns rather than only participating locally.

persuasiveness.rationale: Inferred from her documented role personally negotiating the contracts (wage increases, safety protections, health funds) that ended the five-year Delano strike -- a specific, dated negotiation outcome, not a generic reputation for persuasion.

resourcefulness.rationale: Inferred from documented sustained full-time organizing work while raising a large family (documented to have raised many children across three relationships) -- a specific, sourced logistical pattern rather than a generic claim.

autonomy_need.rationale: Inferred from the documented 1962 decision to leave the Community Service Organization specifically over its unwillingness to advocate for farmworkers, and start a new organization instead of continuing to work within the existing one.

adaptability.rationale: Inferred from the documented shift in tactics across her career -- strike organizing in the 1960s, consumer boycotts in the 1970s, legislative lobbying by 1975, and later foundation-building (2002) -- each a real, dated, different mode of advocacy.

impact_motivation.rationale: Inferred from sustained organizing focus specifically on farmworker welfare across more than five decades, from the 1962 founding through the 2002-founded Dolores Huerta Foundation's active community-center project as of the mid-2020s.

proactive_agency.rationale: Inferred from the documented pattern of initiating new organizing vehicles (the 1962 association, the 2002 foundation) rather than only operating within existing structures.
